bullets: Jun 2026 retail closed at 2,557,234 units with +21.83% YoY growth and +1.03% MoM momentum.
Two-wheelers led volumes at 1,828,458 units (+21.22% YoY), while passenger vehicles hit 410,853 units (+28.63% YoY).
PV inventory stayed healthy at about 33 days, keeping wholesale-retail alignment much tighter than a year ago.
Dealer outlook stayed constructive but measured, with positive demand expectations for both the next month and the next three months.

acma.headline: Indian auto component industry grew 6.8% to Rs 3.56 lakh crore in H1 FY26 — steady demand despite a swing into trade deficit.

metrics.label: Trade balance
metrics.delta: vs USD +150 million surplus in H1 FY25

insights: Industry growth slowed from 9.6% (FY25) to 6.8% (H1 FY26) on softer global demand and selective domestic moderation.
OEM demand still leads, with passenger vehicles and LCVs the strongest contributors.
Aftermarket growth (+9%) outpaced OEM supplies for the first time in several halves — supports the larger-vehicle-parc thesis.
Trade swung from a USD 150M H1 FY25 surplus to a USD 180M H1 FY26 deficit on faster-growing imports — an early warning for ancillary cap-ex priorities.
EV components now contribute 4.6% of total OEM supplies as electrification accelerates.
acma.scope_note: ACMA notes that tyres, batteries, paints and consumables are excluded from industry scope; EV component sales to domestic OEMs are included under OEM supply figures, excluding batteries.
